design_items.statement: The encoder MUST be a pure module that maps a key name plus a modifier state `{ctrl, alt, shift}` plus an `applicationCursor` flag to the exact byte string sent to the PTY.
Arrow keys without modifiers MUST encode as `ESC [ A..D` when `applicationCursor` is false and as `ESC O A..D` when it is true.
Arrows, Home and End with any modifier MUST encode as `ESC [ 1 ; m X` where `m = 1 + shift(1) + alt(2) + ctrl(4)`.
Home and End without modifiers MUST encode as `ESC [ H` / `ESC [ F`, and as `ESC O H` / `ESC O F` when `applicationCursor` is true, matching xterm.js hardware keys.
Insert, Delete, PageUp and PageDown MUST encode as `ESC [ n ~` with n = 2, 3, 5, 6, and as `ESC [ n ; m ~` when a modifier is active.
F1–F4 MUST encode as `ESC O P..S` and F5–F12 as `ESC [ 15~ 17~ 18~ 19~ 20~ 21~ 23~ 24~`.
Esc, Tab, Enter and Backspace MUST encode as `ESC`, `\t`, `\r` and `0x7f`, and Shift+Tab as `ESC [ Z`.

A single character with Ctrl MUST encode per the xterm table: `a`..`z` → `0x01`..`0x1a`; `@`, `2` and Space → `0x00`; `[` and `3` → `0x1b`; `\` and `4` → `0x1c`; `]` and `5` → `0x1d`; `^` and `6` → `0x1e`; `_`, `-` and `7` → `0x1f`; `?` and `8` → `0x7f`; any other character is sent unchanged.
Alt MUST prefix the encoded result with a single `ESC`.
Shift on a single letter MUST upper-case it before Ctrl/Alt are applied.

Encoded bytes MUST reach the server through the existing `TerminalHandle.sendInput` path, which ends in `submitCapturedInput`, so operation IDs, the input queue and the checkpoint barrier apply unchanged.
`TerminalHandle` SHALL expose `getApplicationCursorKeysMode()` that reads the live `term.modes.applicationCursorKeysMode`, forwarded by `TerminalContainer` like `getMouseTrackingActive`.
Each of Ctrl, Alt and Shift MUST hold one of three states: `off`, `once` or `locked`.
A tap MUST move `off` → `once`, `once` → `off` and `locked` → `off`.
A press held for 1500 ms MUST move the key to `locked` at the 1500 ms mark, without waiting for release.
Releasing before 1500 ms MUST count as a tap; a `pointercancel` leaves every state unchanged.
After one encoded key is sent, every modifier in `once` MUST return to `off`, while `locked` modifiers stay `locked`.
Reaching `locked` MUST call `navigator.vibrate(25)` only when that function exists, so a browser without the Vibration API locks silently and raises no error.

heading_path: Applying the latch to system-keyboard input
design_items.statement: When any modifier is not `off`, data from `term.onData` that is exactly one printable ASCII character (0x20–0x7E) MUST be re-encoded through the encoder before `submitCapturedInput`, inside the existing `onData` handler, whatever the IME composition flags say, because Android keyboards deliver Latin letters through composition.

heading_path: Applying the latch to system-keyboard input
design_items.statement: The latch MUST NOT transform non-ASCII data (Hangul syllables and other IME commits), multi-character data, parser replies, focus reports or programmatic paste.

heading_path: Applying the latch to system-keyboard input
design_items.statement: The latch state SHALL live in one module-level store with subscribe/getSnapshot, read by `TerminalView` and by every keyboard component.

heading_path: Applying the latch to system-keyboard input
design_items.statement: The re-encoding MUST happen after the provenance counter (`markUserXtermDataProvenance`) has been consumed and after the query-reply and replay guards have passed, so the re-encoded string is submitted under the original keystroke's permit (REL-BGSTAB-019).
Only Ctrl, Alt and Shift MUST be lockable, each showing a corner dot that is grey when `off`, blue when `once` and glowing orange when `locked`.
The `once` state MUST render as blue text with underline and no filled background, and `locked` as an orange tinted box with an orange border.
While a lockable key is pressed, a fill MUST rise from the bottom over 1500 ms, with the browser context menu, text selection and `contextmenu` propagation to the tab wrapper suppressed.
The bar MUST show, left to right: Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, separator, ←, ↑, ↓, →, separator, Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, and a keyboard-switch button.

The bar MUST render only when `useResponsive().isMobile` is true and either a document-level `focusin` has landed on the active tab's `.xterm-helper-textarea` without a later `focusout`, or the special keyboard is open.
The bar MUST sit directly above the system keyboard, using `window.visualViewport` (height and offsetTop) to compute the keyboard inset.

While the bar is shown, the app root height MUST follow `visualViewport.height` (through a CSS variable on `.app`), so the whole layout including the terminal shrinks above the keyboard and the existing ResizeObserver re-fits xterm.
The bar MUST scroll horizontally when wider than the screen, with its scrollbar hidden.
Every key MUST be at least `--ctl-touch` (44 px) in its smaller tappable dimension in the special keyboard and 36 px high in the bar.
Pressing any bar or panel key MUST NOT move focus away from the terminal while the system keyboard is shown (`preventDefault` on `pointerdown`/`mousedown`).
Win, AltGr, mouse and screenshot keys MUST NOT appear anywhere in the bar or panel.
Tapping the keyboard-switch button while the system keyboard is shown MUST blur the terminal textarea through a new `TerminalHandle.blurInput()` and open the special keyboard panel in the same place.
The panel height MUST equal the last measured system-keyboard inset, with a 280 px default when none was measured.
Tapping the switch button while the panel is open MUST close the panel and call `TerminalHandle.focus()` synchronously inside the tap handler, so iOS and Android raise the system keyboard again.

While the panel is open the terminal textarea MUST stay blurred: the tab wrapper `onPointerDown → focusTerminal` (App.tsx), `TerminalView` `handleClick`, and the pending focus-restore path (`pendingFocusRestoreRef`) are all suppressed, and the blur clears `pendingFocusRestoreRef`.
The panel MUST have a top row Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, Shift and below it three 3×4 blocks: F1–F12; ⌫ / | ~ * - ` : + _ = Enter; and Home ↑ PgUp / ← (empty) → / End ↓ PgDn / Ins Del Numpad.
Every panel key MUST send through the encoder with the latch applied and consume `once` modifiers.
Tapping Numpad MUST replace only the right 3×4 block with `7 8 9 / 4 5 6 / 1 2 3 / 0 . Arrows`, leaving the other blocks in place.
Numpad digits and `.` MUST send as plain characters through the encoder with the latch applied.
The chosen right block SHALL persist per device in `localStorage`, read and written inside try/catch so storage failure changes nothing else.

integration_items.statement: Every user-visible sentence (button titles, aria labels, the switch button label) MUST go through `t()` with keys in both `messages.{en,ko}.json`; key cap names (Ctrl, Esc, F1, PgUp, arrows) stay ASCII constants outside the catalogs.
Desktop behaviour MUST NOT change: no component of this feature renders when `isMobile` is false.
Each sub-issue #134–#138 MUST be closed only after its wave is merged and its requirements carry test evidence.
